change.description: feat(workflow_engine): Add in hook for producing occurrences from the stateful detector
change.author: Cristian Sotomayor

findings.title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is now abstract and cannot be instantiated
findings.body: `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` now inherits from `StatefulDetectorHandler` with only `pass`. It leaves `counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values` and the new `build_occurrence_and_event_data` unimplemented, and all four are `@abc.abstractmethod` (src/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/detector.py:142-170). `MetricAlertFire.detector_handler` points to this class (grouptype.py:27), and `Detector.detector_handler` instantiates it with `group_type.detector_handler(self)` (models/detector.py:86). So any `metric_alert_fire` detector now raises `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class` the moment its handler is read. That aborts `process_detectors` for every detector in the batch. Before this change the handler returned `[]`. A search found no production caller of `process_detectors` yet, so this does not block the merge, but it is wrong as written. Either keep a concrete stub (implement the four members, returning empty or no-op values, with a TODO) or leave it on `DetectorHandler` until the real implementation lands. The `# TODO: This will be a stateful detector` comment on line 10 is also stale now.

findings.title: Occurrence assertions only compare the hard-coded id, so they verify almost nothing
findings.body: `IssueOccurrence.__eq__` compares only `id` (src/sentry/issues/issue_occurrence.py:181-184). `build_mock_occurrence_and_event` always uses the same id (`eb4b0acf...`), so every `== DetectorEvaluationResult(..., result=occurrence, ...)` assertion passes no matter what fingerprint, type or priority the handler produced. This already hides a mistake in this diff: `TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe` builds the expected occurrence for group key `"val1"` (line 536-538) but evaluates `"group_key"` (line 548), so the fingerprints differ (`<id>:val1` vs `<id>:group_key`) and the test still passes. Likewise, in `test_state_results_multi_group`, `occurrence` and `occurrence_2` are equal to each other, and so are `event_data` and `event_data_2`. The `assert_has_calls(..., any_order=True)` (line 206-222) therefore cannot tell group_1's occurrence from group_2's. Derive the id from the group key in the mock (e.g. a hash of the fingerprint), or compare `fingerprint` and `initial_issue_priority` explicitly. Then fix the `"val1"`/`"group_key"` mismatch.

findings.title: Docstring still says evaluate returns a list
findings.body: `evaluate` now returns `dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]`, but the docstring still says it "returns a list of `DetectorEvaluationResult`".

contracts.action: StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate_group_key_value calls the new abstract hook build_occurrence_and_event_data for non-OK status changes
contracts.equivalent_path: The OK branch builds a StatusChangeMessage inline (detector.py:290-297)
contracts.before_after: Before, non-OK results carried result=None and were skipped by process_detectors. Now they carry an IssueOccurrence, and process_detectors sends it to Kafka through create_issue_occurrence_from_result (detector.py:60-62, 73-87). PriorityLevel(new_status) is safe because the OK value is excluded and the LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH values match PriorityLevel (workflow_engine/types.py:8-12, types/group.py:63-66).
contracts.visible_effect: Issue occurrences are produced for detectors that go active
contracts.failure_mode: If a subclass does not implement the hook, instantiation raises TypeError. MetricAlertDetectorHandler is such a subclass (incidents/grouptype.py:11-12, 27), and its handler is created at models/detector.py:86.

contracts.before_after: Same lookup, now reused by detector_handler
contracts.failure_mode: Returns None for an unknown slug; detector_handler logs the error and returns None (models/detector.py:65-74)

summary: The change switches detector results from a list to a dict keyed by group key and adds an abstract `build_occurrence_and_event_data` hook so stateful detectors produce real occurrences. Two problems. First, `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` now inherits from `StatefulDetectorHandler` without implementing its abstract members, so creating the handler for any `metric_alert_fire` detector raises TypeError (I found no production caller of `process_detectors` yet). Second, the new tests compare `IssueOccurrence` objects, and those compare only `id`, which the mock hard-codes. The occurrence assertions therefore verify almost nothing, and they already hide a group-key mismatch in `TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe` and identical occurrences in the multi-group test. One docstring is stale.
